rationale: The exact version is upheld with the date-boundary and search qualifications stated here. The entire printed page 76 contains one permission: the quarterly session ordinarily held October 1 under the April 1, 1905 order may instead be held at the Governor office on the Isthmus on November 15, 1906. The page is signed Theodore Roosevelt, President, and dated September 20, 1906. This changes one session date; it creates no perpetual revised quarterly calendar and no independent session-duration command. The day specified is included in the permission, so November 16 is the first civil date after its temporal window, equivalent to the close of November 15. The supported ending is expiration of this scheduling permission, not a finding of meeting performance or adjournment.
operative_inventory: One complete operative paragraph, excluding metadata and signature from the inventory scope, with full date/signature separately checked. Place and date are conditions of the same permission, not independent continuing mandates. No appointment, report, recurring regulation or separate prospective command appears. Permitted identity crosswalk entry 44 links the September 20 date and quarterly-session subject to EO506; the source prints no EO number.
effective_date_and_earlier_candidates: The permission is issued September 20, 1906, but is exercisable for the named November 15 session and is not exhausted merely by issuance. October 1 is the displaced ordinary date, not a first cessation. November 15 cannot be wholly excluded without nullifying the expressly authorized day. The exact source prints a calendar day, not an express midnight timestamp or time-zone rule: November 16 00:00 local is the civil-date boundary convention, not independently observed event evidence. An earlier actual exercise, meeting or adjournment has not been shown and is not inferred. No examined source establishes an intervening earlier revocation; bounded searches do not prove its universal absence.
parent_scope_analysis: All of the April 1, 1905 parent order through its Roosevelt signature on printed pages 33-36 (PDF46-49) was visually inspected. Printed33 separately sets quarterly sessions and provides that each session continues as public business requires, with additional rules for special sessions, quorum and governance. Printed34-36 contain departmental, appointments, contracts, reporting and other parent duties; those are not new EO506 commands. The parent also preserves other prior Canal orders insofar as consistent; that parent clause neither is an EO506 savings clause nor permits a new EO506 calendar substitution after November15. The separate War Department letter beginning below the parent signature on printed36 was distinguished from the parent order.
savings_and_residuals: No express savings or continuing independent EO506 duty is printed. If a session validly commenced under the date substitution, its possible continuation is governed by the parent rule; expiry of fresh scheduling permission does not terminate the session or invalidate its acts. Neither actual convening nor actual adjournment, and no duration of an actual session, is found. Historical validity and other parent consequences are retained as consequences rather than counted as live EO506 scheduling power.
